lesson.applicability: On-demand review of strict canonical integer/ratio input boundaries.
lesson.cause: A literal constructor sighting is insufficient without the declared input contract and independent deciding check.
lesson.correction: Attach the concrete exact-parser review prompt, inspect the harmful and benign cases, and request an independent bounded checker when defect admission is needed. Keep this candidate inert.
lesson.counterexample: The historical repair adds pre-construction grammar checks and a legitimate large-cost control; the original exponent failure and the valid ratio case need different dispositions.
lesson.evidence_excerpt: Exact string type, input-length and ASCII integer-or-ratio syntax checks precede Fraction construction.
lesson.exceptions: Constructor text alone is not a defect. Explicitly bounded alternative grammars and prior lexical admission are benign; a prompt never supplies the independent danger signal.
lesson.failed_claim: A parser constructor call or a prompt warning alone proves the parser safe or activates an antibody.
lesson.verification: Read the complete Round 2 code repair review and retained resource-probe outputs. Compilation checks only source/prompt custody and literal example separation, not semantic detector accuracy or historical replay.
